headline: CPI ran hot and December hike odds hit 85%; BTC fell to 0.8% above its 200-day average as short-term holders turned to heavy loss-taking.
summary: Loss-taking passed from long-term to short-term holders: short-term holders moved into concentrated loss-taking while LTH-SOPR climbed back to 1.00. October CPI rose 0.4%, above forecasts, and the 10-year yield touched 5% intraday. The close is only 0.8% above the 200-day average, with an estimated long-liquidation band at 71–72.6K below; the hedge needs 5 straight closes under the average.

overview.lead: Selling has moved onto short-term holders, and macro piled on: a hot CPI locked in a December hike and pushed BTC to the edge of its 200-day average.
points: Short-term holders moved into concentrated loss-taking on Nov 10 while long-term holders stopped (first finding).
Short-term holder supply between 72K and 66K is thin; the next thick layer sits at 62–66K (second finding).
Leverage has not left: open interest is 345,129 BTC and three-venue funding is 10.0%.
PPI on Friday, FOMC minutes next Wednesday.

cycle.lead: Bull day 33 with still only one evidence light on; the cycle gauges did not weaken further on this drop, and the dawn index stays at Daybreak.
points: 62 straight closes above a rising 200-day average, bull day 33; the average was 71,980 thirty days ago and is still rising.
Only 1 of 6 evidence lights is on (realized cap +0.26% over 30 days); 12-month momentum, MVRV vs its 1-year average, exchange supply, short-term holder cost, and cost vs true market mean are all off.
The weekly regime score is 0.21, still early bull; the dawn index is at Daybreak with heat 35. Both lean weak, in the same direction.
At the last 30 days' pace, a straight-line extrapolation puts the short-term holder cost crossing above the true market mean near Dec 18, 5 days later than yesterday's estimate.

market.lead: The current up-leg is on the edge of ending: the close is 0.1% above the leg's end line at 73,605, and sell pressure hit 100, the first bottom combo since the algorithm change.
points: The leg started at 58,532 on Jun 30, ran 133 days to a high of 86,594, and is now 14.9% off that high; a little lower and it becomes a 15% reversal.

Sell pressure 100, momentum quality 0.20. After the 20 past bottom combos, price was up 11 times 30 days later with a +1.8% median, about the same as any day; after May 2022 it was still down 37% 90 days later.
Volume was 1.47 times the 20-day average and the close sat at 41% of the day's range.

deriv.lead: The post-CPI drop did not flush leverage: open interest rose again, only $86.8M of longs were liquidated, and the liquidation band is still waiting below.
points: Open interest is 345,129 BTC, the 98th percentile since 2021; up 13% in 30 days while price fell 12%.
Five-venue weighted funding is 7.1%, with OKX and Hyperliquid both at 11.0%; compared with yesterday on the three-venue basis it went 8.2% → 10.0%.

The estimated long-liquidation band is 71.0–72.6K, 2.7% below the close, about 25,000 BTC (estimate, seven venues via Coinalyze); a move there would trigger a batch of market sells that could speed up a decline.
The 25-delta risk reversal widened from −3.0 to −3.8, so puts got pricier; DVOL at 39.5 did not rise, so traders are buying direction protection rather than volatility.

flows.lead: US money is still leaving while Asia pays a premium: Coinbase spot net-sold 3,382 BTC in a week, and the Korea premium rose to 1.55%.
points: ETF data delayed: the latest complete day is Nov 5, 3 trading days behind. Seven trading days show −$1.36B to Nov 5 (The Block); Nov 6 provisional −$412M and Nov 9 provisional −$201M (Farside, SoSoValue).
The Coinbase premium is −0.133% daily and −0.137% on a 7-day average; US buyers are still at a discount.
Stablecoins total $292.0B, down $14.1B in 30 days.
Realized cap is +0.26% over 30 days, still a small inflow; the 10-year real yield is 2.66% (Nov 9).

onchain.lead: The main loss-takers have changed: STH-SOPR has been below 1 for 5 days, and network-wide realized loss of $1.04B was bigger than at the Sep 15 low.
points: This page's findings: short-term holders capitulating while long-term holders stopped (first finding); thin supply below 72K (second finding).
Only 27% of short-term holders are in profit; their realized loss was 4,504 BTC, 12% more than yesterday (CheckOnChain, Nov 10).
Network profit ÷ loss has a 7-day average of 0.59; at that pace the 90-day average drops back below 1 around Jan 3, 2027 (in Dec 2019 it also fell back below 1 after 7 months above).
The 7-day hashrate average is 958 EH/s, a bit lower again; the Nov 13 difficulty estimate is −7.1%.

news.title: US October CPI rose 0.4% and core 0.3%, both 0.1 point above forecasts; BTC broke below 73,000 intraday, its lowest since Aug 20
news.read: A December hike went from 80% priced to fully priced; the open question is 25 or 50 basis points. BTC closed at 73,700 with the 200-day average at 73,137, 0.8% below; its 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.70, so it follows stocks down. Event risk; it does not change the market stage, but it brings the hedge line close.

news.title: CME FedWatch: odds of no December hike fell to zero, 85% for 25 bp and 15% for 50 bp; Fed Governor Waller said 50 bp should be considered if inflation stays stubborn
news.read: The hike is priced; the new variable is size. A hot PPI on Friday would push the 15% for 50 bp higher. A 2.66% real yield (Nov 9) is a headwind. Does not affect the cycle reading.

news.title: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.015% intraday and the 2-year to 4.757%, up 15 and 21 bp on the day; Nvidia closed down 5% at $168.91
news.read: The short end rose more than the long end, so hike expectations are the driver, not growth. Our FRED data shows 4.88% through Nov 9 and has not caught this jump. BTC has followed stocks down this week but not up, so more Nvidia weakness is pressure. Does not change on-chain readings.

news.title: Spot BTC ETFs saw $201M of net outflows on Nov 9, a third straight outflow day; BlackRock's IBIT alone lost $213M, total assets $94.43B
news.read: Half the previous day's outflow, but the same direction. We logged Nov 9 as provisional −$201M (Farside via CoinDesk and SoSoValue agree); The Block will overwrite it. Seven complete trading days total −$1.36B to Nov 5. Does not affect the market stage.

news.title: Miner MARA disclosed selling 13,597 BTC, about $1.1B, over the past six weeks and said it will sell more
news.read: About 320 BTC a day over six weeks, roughly 70% of the 453 BTC mined network-wide each day: a real seller. With the 7-day hashrate at 958 EH/s and a −7.1% difficulty estimate for Nov 13, this kind of selling can grow when miner revenue is squeezed. Does not affect the cycle reading.

news.title: About $200M of leveraged positions were liquidated within five minutes of the CPI release; ETH, XRP and SOL each fell about 6% intraday
news.read: Most liquidations were in altcoins; across our five venues, BTC long liquidations on Nov 10 were only $86.8M and open interest rose by about 2,700 BTC. Leverage was not flushed, and the estimated 71.0–72.6K band is still there. Does not affect the market stage.

news.title: Santiment: BTC has lost about 108,700 non-empty addresses since Oct 16
news.read: Addresses are not people, and exchange wallet consolidation also cuts the count. In our address cohorts the 1–10 BTC tier added 7,070 BTC in 30 days, so small holders are not leaving. Does not change the on-chain reading.

findings.title: Loss-taking relay: long-term holders stopped, short-term holders capitulate
findings.lean_why: Lower price with bigger loss-taking means selling is still growing; the size is half the Jun 30 low, so sellers do not look exhausted yet.
findings.what: The people selling at a loss are now short-term holders: their loss-taking intensity rose to 2.7, the second concentrated episode in 11 days, while LTH-SOPR rose back from 0.82 to 1.00 (Bitview, Nov 10).
findings.why: Split by cohort, the two sides moved in opposite directions. Short-term holders realized losses equal to 0.14% of their own realized cap in a day, against 0.04% in profits (Bitview); CheckOnChain agrees, with realized loss at 4,504 BTC, 22% more than a week ago, and STH-SOPR below 1 for 5 days. The network confirms it: realized loss of $1.04B, 6.99 bp of market cap, larger than the 5.41 bp at the Sep 15 low, at a lower price. Long-term holders stopped, with 7-day realized loss at $1.39B, $0.1B less than yesterday. Our sell-pressure gauge hit 100 with momentum at 0.20 the same day; three separate methods point to growing short-term selling.
findings.alt: LTH-SOPR jumped from 0.82 back to 1.00 in one day, so part of yesterday's heavy loss may have been large old-coin moves that per-UTXO data cannot tell from internal transfers; on the short-term side we used both Bitview and CheckOnChain and compare only direction. Loss intensity is measured against its own last 105 days, and loss-taking has been light for months, so the bar is lower too.
findings.history: Lower price with bigger loss-taking has often come late in declines, though not always the last time; about 20 cases since 2013. Concentrated short-term loss-taking above the 200-day average happened 40 times; 30 days later price was up 24 times with a +3.8% median, close to any day's 59% and +4.7%. This cycle's real lows had much larger losses: 13.2 bp on Jun 30 and 47.2 bp on Feb 5.
findings.so: Yesterday we wrote that short-term holders were not capitulating; correction today: they have moved into concentrated loss-taking. The chain is that long-term holders stopped first, so the old-coin capitulation did not spread; short-term holders followed, but at half the Jun 30 size, so seller exhaustion is not in place yet. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: Two paths by Nov 17: short-term holder realized loss above 5,000 BTC means the capitulation is widening toward full-size, confirming; a close back above the short-term holder cost of 75,717 means this selling hit a low and was absorbed, refuting.

findings.title: Supply is thin from 72K to 66K; the next thick layer is 62–66K
findings.lean_why: An estimated long-liquidation band starts 2.7% below the close, and there is no thick supply to absorb selling down to 66K, so price can move quickly; on the plus side, no large new group gets trapped there.
findings.what: Below 72K there is almost no short-term holder supply until 66K: at 72K, 2.69M BTC of short-term holder coins would be underwater, and at 66K only 2.76M (CheckOnChain, Nov 10).
findings.why: The question: if the 200-day average breaks, where is the next defended level? On the cost map, the two thickest short-term holder buckets are 76K and 80K, both above the close; the first thick bucket below is 62K at about 460K BTC. URPD agrees: the 72–74K bucket holds only 155K BTC, and the nearest cluster below is 64–66K at 556K BTC (Nov 9). Derivatives sit on top: the estimated long-liquidation band is 71.0–72.6K, with the 200-day average at 73,137 just above it. Only at 64K does short-term holder underwater supply jump by 400K BTC; long-term holder losses rise evenly, from 5.81M BTC at 72K to 6.76M at 66K.
findings.alt: Thin supply does not guarantee a fast move: about 950K BTC of long-term holder coins would fall into loss between 72K and 66K, and whether they sell depends on LTH-SOPR. The liquidation band is an estimate with assumed leverage, so its position shifts with the assumptions; URPD lags a day.
findings.history: Supply concentration within ±5% of price is only 7.5%, the 36th percentile since 2018, so not crowded; the median largest move over the next 30 days is 15.8% on ordinary days and 22.3% on the most crowded 10%.
findings.so: The chain: short-term holders trapped above 72K are already taking losses (first finding), so a break of 72K would not force out a large new batch of short-term sellers; but nothing thick sits above 66K to absorb selling, so support depends on the 62–66K layer and long-term holders. The framework watches the 200-day average and acts only after 5 straight closes below 73,137.
findings.next: By Nov 17: a close below 72,000 means the 200-day average and the liquidation band both failed and price entered the thin zone, confirming; a close back above 76,000, the thickest short-term holder cost bucket, refutes.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 46
items.points: BTC near 75K, closing at its lowest since August; spot CVD −$91.8M; futures OI $37.0B, down only 1.1%, with long funding payments still above the high band; 25-delta skew 11.1%, strong demand for downside protection; weekly ETF outflows $1.6B and ETF MVRV 1.30, below its low band; short-term holders slipped into a small unrealized loss on Sunday; realized P/L ratio −0.63. Conclusion: defensive positioning and crowded longs, but some leverage has been flushed and momentum no longer confirms the decline.
items.meaning: "Crowded longs" matches our data (open interest at the 98th percentile, 73.7% of Binance accounts long), but we see leverage added back on Nov 9, so "some leverage flushed" doesn't hold yet. Its $1.6B weekly ETF outflow and SoSoValue's $1.28B use different definitions.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Idling at Support
items.points: True Market Mean 77.7K, short-term holder cost 75.7K, with the 200-day average inside a 73–76K band; long liquidation risk at 73–76K and 60–63K; holding 73–76K is a healthy reset, while a break below 73K points to longer consolidation.
items.meaning: The Nov 9 intraday low of 73,602 touched the band's lower edge and recovered; the 75,253 close is still inside. Its "below 73K" nearly coincides with our hedge line at 73,156.

items.title: Another resilience test: The Midterms are here
